_note: うどんの系譜。品目ハブ（/en/eat/udon/）の表と各系譜ページがここから描く。planned の行の era は出典が付くまで「—」
name: Udon

origin.era: Edo period; legend from the 9th c.

cells.noodle: Thick, square-cut, foot-kneaded, firm and springy; 40%+ water, 3%+ salt, rested 2 hours (the 'Honba Sanuki' standard)
cells.broth: Iriko (dried anchovy) from the Inland Sea, light soy from Shōdoshima
cells.topping: Spring onion, ginger, tempura you pick yourself
cells.howToEat: Self-service: warm your own noodles, choose hot/cold noodle and broth (atsu-atsu, hiya-atsu…), kake, bukkake, kama-age, kama-tama

cells.broth: 'Sume': kelp and bonito with flying fish or anchovy, light soy, slightly sweet
cells.howToEat: Fast; a merchant's lunch. Some chains let you choose softness

cells.noodle: Soft, chewy, not too thick — made to carry the broth
cells.broth: Ma-kombu kelp and dried fish, light soy; pale and clear
cells.topping: Sweet-simmered fried tofu (kitsune); 'tanuki' here means that tofu on soba
cells.howToEat: Drink the broth; udon-suki hotpot in winter

cells.noodle: Thick and soft, boiled for a long time
cells.broth: No broth: a small pool of dark tamari-soy sauce with bonito
cells.howToEat: Mix and eat; the pilgrim's quick meal at the shrine

origin.era: Early Edo period (founder and dates differ by source)

cells.noodle: Dried, thin and flat; hand-twisted on two rods, pressed flat and stretched by hand over 3–4 days; no oil. Method made public in 1972
cells.broth: Strong soy dip with bonito stock, or sesame-miso; also hot broth
cells.howToEat: Rinsed in cold water, then cold with a dip or hot; locally, short 'mago-udon' for babies and the elderly

origin.era: Said to have come with the envoy ships to Tang China (unproven)

cells.noodle: Dried, hand-stretched, round, about 1.7 mm; camellia oil brushed on while stretching
cells.broth: Ago (flying-fish) stock dip, often with egg and soy
cells.topping: Spring onion, bonito flakes, raw egg; yuzu-koshō, ginger
cells.howToEat: Jigoku-daki: lifted straight from a bubbling iron pot into the dip; chilled zaru in summer

origin.era: Meiji era (farm ministry); from hōtō (Cultural Agency)

cells.noodle: Flour and water only, no salt; stays firm when simmered
cells.howToEat: Simmered and served in an earthenware pot

cells.noodle: Flat, about 1 mm thick and 7–8 mm wide
cells.broth: Traditionally muroaji fish stock and tamari; now dashi and soy
cells.topping: Nagoya's red fish cake; curry or mochi versions

cells.noodle: Wide, flat, not rested, simmered raw
cells.broth: Miso with niboshi stock; the flour thickens it
cells.howToEat: Big pot at home, an iron pot per person in restaurants

cells.noodle: Torn or stretched flour dumplings; noodle-like 'nobe-dago' in Aso
cells.topping: Burdock, radish, carrot; often sweet potato in Kumamoto
cells.howToEat: Everyday home food; especially autumn and winter
